title: Birds of the Brush takes flight for 15th annual art competition
excerpt: The Birds of the Brush art competition is back for its 15th year, inviting artists and photographers to celebrate the birds of the Rio Grande ahead of the Laredo Birding Festival in February.
content:
The Birds of the Brush art competition is back for its 15th year, inviting artists and photographers to celebrate the birds of the Rio Grande, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The contest is held alongside the annual Laredo Birding Festival, which returns for its 15th year Feb. 3-6, 2027. The festival is organized by the Rio Grande International Study Center, with professional field guides and members of the local Monte Mucho Audubon Society leading birders on trips along Laredo's riverfront, creek systems, nature trails and private ranchland.

Each year the contest showcases how Laredo's river ecosystem draws hundreds of bird species, some migrating from as far as Canada and the Central American tropics. Past editions have invited artists, photographers, teachers and students to submit work, with the artwork displayed at the Laredo Center for the Arts.

Laredo sits in one of the birdiest corridors in North America, home to species including the Morelet's seedeater, green parakeets, Altamira orioles and four species of kingfisher. A sneak peek at this year's Birds of the Brush contest is part of the festival program.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 13, 2026; Laredo Birding Festival (laredobirdingfestival.org).
